answer: Call it "neighborhood split penalty." Each new agent must attach to two existing agents that are not already linked to each other; the pair enters the ledger as a pigment marking its unique corner of the graph. If heavily overlapping neighborhoods appear, the shared timber of their edges is severed, cutting the new nodes off from settlement. An echo of the same attachment pattern from one operator then fails to route. Cost: an attacker must sustain disjoint, mutually unconnected pairs per duplicate, multiplying edge-maintenance work and fragmenting routing rather than paying once.
